assessments.task: Identify the four atlas parathyroid targets and distinguish upper from lower pairs in a posterior thyroid locator.

axes.observation: Clean imports of the two variants agree at all gland vertices exactly. Both upper centroids are 19.80 mm above the lower centroids in the same native frame. The owner independently bound the thyroid and targets to the native atlas.
The four mirrored markers are visibly simplified in both side views. The source thyroid contains a prominent central projection of unassigned identity.

The posterior panel distinguishes right and left, upper and lower. Both labeled side views show the same targets behind the same-source thyroid surface. The component alone gives no thyroid placement cue.
Four selectable 128-triangle markers and one 2,600-triangle thyroid mesh support the exercise. The portable companion is 59,456 bytes.

assessments.task: Scrub the schematic heartbeat and distinguish ventricular contour change from a rigid shift of the whole heart.

axes.observation: The selected LV morph, input times, values, aortic mesh and source root retain exact streams. Twenty integer-frame evaluations match control world vertices exactly. Maximum sampled wall change is 5.047 mm and aortic change is zero.
The neutral same-frame comparison shows the ventricular tip move relative to the fixed aortic reference. The source full-heart reverse view remains available for vessel profiles.
The phase comparison and retained 0.8-second clip expose ventricular contour change against a stationary aorta. The complete atlas supplies context.
Three material primitives on two selectable parts replace the full 247-mesh delivery for this task. 222,336 triangles become 30,646 and 8,180,224 bytes become 1,158,724.

assessments.task: Compare expiration to peak inspiration and point out the descending diaphragm dome, descending lung bases and liver shift.

axes.observation: All retained world vertices match the delivered assembly in each of 121 integer frames. Measured descent from frame 1 to 49 is 20.90 mm at the dome crest, 17.60 mm at the left lower-lobe base and 7.98 mm at the inferior liver.
At both phases the neutral side view shows the curved crest, retained open rim and source lobe edge. The dome flattens and the rim remains visible in isolation.
The matched phase and diaphragm-only cards expose the crest shift and reveal the lung and liver motion, keeping the frame and camera fixed.
Seven selectable objects retain 93,502 of 245,126 triangles. The focused compressed Blender file uses 8,340,874 bytes. The checked reduction does not change required movement.

assessments.task: Find the bladder base, neck and paired ureteral entry landmarks in same-atlas context.

axes.observation: All retained mesh vertices, buffers and ancestor transforms match the same-atlas control exactly. Both small orifice patches, base, neck, dome and trigone retain distinct selectable surfaces.
Removing neighboring pelvic organs makes the whole bladder outline recognizable. In the opposite oblique the patch edge and retained source ridge are visible separately from the neck and dome.
The rear focus shows the two tiny landmarks against the retained ureters and base. The opposite oblique shows the basin and retained root shape.
Eight task-relevant primitives retain 69,186 of 120,796 triangles and 1,271,856 of 2,449,600 bytes. The ureters orient both entry landmarks and the dome supports intact-form comparison.
